findings.title: Silence drawer can never open when only promRule is provided
findings.body: The 'Silence notifications' menu item is shown based on promRule abilities (canSilence can be true via the new useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities path), and clicking it calls setShowSilenceDrawer(true). However, the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is truthy, where `rule` is the RulerRuleDTO prop. In the new list view (FilterView -> GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons), only `promRule` is passed and `rule` is undefined, so the drawer is never rendered: clicking 'Silence notifications' silently does nothing. The silence action is broken for all Grafana-managed rules in the alert list.

findings.title: Delete menu item is never rendered in the new alert list view
findings.body: The Delete item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`, and its click handler requires a RulerRuleDTO (`handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier)`). In the new list view GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule (no ruler rule is fetched anymore), so rulerRule is undefined and users with delete permission lose the Delete action entirely for Grafana-managed rules in the list. The delete-ability checks via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities become dead code. If deletion is meant to remain available, the menu must construct the deletion from the identifier/promRule; if it is intentionally removed, the tests asserting delete presence for Grafana rules (RulesTable.test.tsx 'Should render Delete button for users with the delete permission') contradict this behavior.

findings.title: Pause action is never rendered in the new alert list view
findings.body: The pause menu item requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` to be truthy in addition to canPause. Since the list view no longer fetches ruler rules, rulerRule is undefined and the Pause action is missing from the menu for Grafana-managed rules, even though the code computes a grafana pause ability (grafanaPauseSupported/grafanaPauseAllowed) specifically for this view. The new pause-ability path is dead code and users lose the ability to pause/unpause rules from the list.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem is rendered without a React key in the rules list
findings.body: In the rules.map switch, the 'grafana' case renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without a `key` prop (the old code used `key={key}`), while the 'datasource' and default cases still pass keys. Rendering list children without keys causes React reconciliation problems (element re-use across filter updates/infinite scroll, full re-mounts, state loss in menus/drawers) and React key warnings. The `key={key}` should be restored on the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

findings.title: Federated rule group support silently dropped from ruler abilities
findings.body: The refactored useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with only a TODO comment, whereas the previous useAllAlertRuleAbilities computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. For Mimir/Metrics Enterprise data sources with federated rule groups (source_tenants set), immutableRule is now false, so the Update/Delete/Pause/Restore abilities will report these rules as editable/deletable when they are not. This is a behavior regression for cloud rules (rules in federated groups get edit/delete UI they previously did not).
